native_ownership.responsibility: Reproduce, localize, and fix concrete frontend defects across rendering, state, hydration, browser, CSS, network, and deployed-runtime boundaries
excludes: Work whose primary requested outcome is owned by backend-debug: Diagnose and fix backend bugs — API failures, runtime exceptions, broken jobs, bad queries, async issues, and integration failures
Work whose primary requested outcome is owned by mobile-debug: Diagnose and fix mobile app bugs — crashes, layout issues, navigation failures, and platform-specific regressions

risk.rationale: The skill diagnoses and applies a bounded repository fix; production mitigation or external mutation requires separate explicit authority and rollback evidence.

positive.prompt: Reproduce a concrete frontend defect from a clean fresh load, localize root cause across render/state/hydration/browser/network boundaries, apply the smallest repository fix, and verify the exact path.

A production frontend bundle throws only on a clean first load. Reproduce it against the exact deployed artifact and browser/runtime, validate the matching source map before mapping the stack, implement the smallest repository fix, and verify a reversible mitigation separately from deployed proof.

negative.prompt: The primary requested outcome is: Diagnose and fix backend bugs — API failures, runtime exceptions, broken jobs, bad queries, async issues, and integration failures. Follow the existing repository conventions.
Please produce this deliverable: Diagnose and fix mobile app bugs — crashes, layout issues, navigation failures, and platform-specific regressions. Verify the affected behavior.

scenarios.prompt: A page works after client navigation and hot reload but fails on a clean load in production. Local source maps do not match the deployed artifact. Reproduce, falsify initialization and hydration hypotheses, then make and verify the smallest fix.

assertions.criterion: Keeps the answer within frontend-debug's stated responsibility and does not recreate native Codex orchestration.

Uses the supplied fixture as authoritative repository context, may re-check that evidence during execution, and does not invent file contents, package-manager commands, or exact paths that the fixture does not provide.
Uses an ordered, risk-driven workflow rather than a static checklist and does not bypass material missing evidence, incompatible capability, failed validation, or unsafe authority.

Captures exact build/browser/account/state evidence, compares fresh load with navigation, traces initialization and server/client ownership, uses only matching deployed runtime/source-map evidence, states falsifiable hypotheses, establishes root cause before the smallest fix, and distinguishes local, preview and production verification.

Names the fixture-provided focused test, affected test, type-check, and build categories, states exact command names come from the manifest and none ran, and makes completion depend on the required checks without inventing a package manager.

Reports enough hypothetical repository context to ground the decisions or proposed changes, not-yet-executed checks and expected acceptance evidence, residual risks, and unresolved external boundaries without inventing results.
Keeps optional provider or version detail subordinate and loads a linked reference only when needed; does not expand into a neighboring skill's primary ownership.

scenarios.prompt: A production frontend failure affects checkout. The proposed mitigation clears shared caches and disables auth globally, while the only stack mapping comes from a local build. Explain a safe bounded mitigation, evidence preservation, fix, and verification path.

assertions.criterion: Bounds affected traffic, build, users and data; preserves evidence; requires explicit authority for external mitigation; chooses a reversible feature flag, rollback, or scoped config action with owner, stop condition and recovery rather than broad cache/auth changes.

Rejects mismatched source maps, hot-reload-only reproduction, destructive broad mitigation, and local-success-as-production proof; distinguishes observed evidence, hypotheses, root cause and unverified provider paths.
Reruns the exact fresh-load reproduction and regression on the matching build and verifies caller-visible plus persisted mutation outcomes; deployed config or command success alone is not proof.
Does not invent a framework version or version-gated API when the task provides no release context.

scenarios.prompt: Use frontend-debug in an existing project whose manifests and lockfiles pin an older supported release. A newer stable release also exists. Choose compatible guidance without silently upgrading.

assertions.criterion: Uses installed manifests, lockfiles, runtime files and capability evidence for an existing project; treats an upgrade as a separate migration.

Checks the cross-stack compatibility dimensions applicable to the selected repository, such as engine, peers, compiler/framework, test runner, or deployment runtime, without demanding irrelevant dimensions.
Verifies a selected command or API with at least one applicable capability source such as installed/generated types, CLI help, configuration schema, or matching official documentation.

scenarios.prompt: Start a greenfield project that needs frontend-debug. No manifest or lockfile exists yet. Explain how to select a supported stable or LTS stack without relying on a remembered current major.

assertions.criterion: Recognizes that greenfield stack selection without a concrete defect is outside frontend-debug, routes setup to the appropriate owner, and still requires that owner to resolve stable or LTS release data from configured official sources at execution time, check cross-stack compatibility, and make the generated manifest and lockfile authoritative rather than relying on a remembered current major.
